newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Greenpeace launches PVC-free credit card in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace launches PVC-free credit card in Brazil.

text.p: Following Greenpeace in Great Britain, the group in Brazil and a local bank on Thursday said they launched an environment-friendly credit card almost entirely free of the polluting plastic PVC.

The Greenpeace credit card, developed with Banco Excel Economico, is made of Biopol, a biodegradable material produced from cereal plants, the partners said in a statement. "This initiative is an opportunity for the bank to advance environmental goals through our commercial and financial activities," Excel Economico president Ezequiel Nasser said in the statement.
Excel Economico also launched the "Greenpeace Bank Account," with checkbooks to be made with non-chlorine bleached paper and illustrated with Greenpeace images, the statement said.
Up to now, all checkbooks in Brazil are totally made with chlorine bleached paper, it added.
Greenpeace Brazil also announced licensing agreements with seven other companies, including a department store with 16 branches across the country, and a large publishing house.
"The licensed products are examples of how Greenpeace can stimulate industry and services sectors to move to cleaner activities," said Roberto Kishinami, executive director at Greenpeace Brazil.
Greenpeace said there are around 17 million PVC credit cards in use in Brazil and this number is expected to increase to 24.5 million by the end of the year.
It also said the Biopol plastic is 100 percent free of PVC but the magnetic strip on the back of the card and some of the inks still contain traces of the plastic.
The PVC-free card was first launched in Britain early last month with Co-Operative Bank Plc.
